challenge.method: I tested whether the documentary role relied on treating a governing license as a second witness, or on attributing the SPDX title to the publisher. I compared the LICENSE heading, notice, disclaimer, grant, each numbered condition and contact block with the README notice and the decoded SPDX licenseText. I checked the SPDX template for title and notice variations, the tag object and payload for the target type and SHA, and the README for limits on third-party rights.
challenge.results: The documentary role is defensible because the proposition asks what the publisher placed in one identified file. Its heading is “Copyright notice:”. The README repeats the notice, and SPDX supplies the title “zlib License”. The disclaimer, grant and all three restrictions agree in wording after allowing for whitespace. SPDX marks the title optional and the copyright field variable. Its licenseText omits the release-specific notice and contact block, so a whole-file byte identity claim would fail. The tag target matches the commit used to retrieve both publisher files. The README expressly disclaims conveyance of third-party intellectual-property rights. These differences and limits leave the scoped release-reference finding intact.

limitations: v1.4 identifies the software release. The evidence establishes no separately versioned license edition. “active” is the proposed index lifecycle state, outside the publisher’s and SPDX’s authority for this claim.

The finding is limited to the pinned release reference. It establishes neither identity across all releases or variants nor a grant covering independently licensed material. The grant addresses “this software”. The sources establish no separate permission to reuse or relicense the license text itself.
The governing-text and documentary views of LICENSE share the same location, bytes and origin. The README also shares the publisher’s origin. No independent corroboration is claimed.

GitHub reports the tag signature as unverified with reason “bad_email”. The tag-target finding rests on the repository’s annotated tag object. The adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce was supplied as a pin and was not independently recomputed.
reasoning: The root LICENSE at commit 99623ef7097352da7993ba614161fd6a311e046e records the 1995–2026 copyright notice for Jean-loup Gailly and Mark Adler and contains three numbered restrictions. The publisher’s annotated v1.4 tag targets that commit. These facts support using this exact file as the release reference for the index record. The name “zlib License” comes from the pinned SPDX record, whose identifier is “Zlib”.
